claims.claim: New experts initialize zero-delta and are never copied from prior experts.
claims.detail: LoRAExpert sets B=zeros and A=kaiming_uniform_(a=sqrt(5)); forward is x -> A -> B so the appended expert's delta output is exactly zero at init; add_expert() is called with no copy_from in both methods, and the independent method rebuilds the model from base weights. Caveat: the A matrices are drawn from the global torch RNG, so bitwise-identical experts require the same (seed, stream position); distribution and protocol are identical. Empirically confirmed below: position-matched banks produce bitwise-equal own-expert diagonal scores, and first-task (position 0) streams are byte-identical to independent runs.

claims.claim: Backbone and old experts are frozen; only the newest expert is trainable; optimizer state is per-phase.
claims.detail: add_expert/train_expert call _freeze_all (requires_grad_(False) plus grad clears); train_expert refuses any index except the newest; optimizer_step aborts if any frozen parameter acquires a gradient; make_optimizer receives only requires_grad parameters and is rebuilt fresh for every phase, so optimizer moments never carry across tasks or methods. Run-time stage_resources show trainable == active_trainable at every stage (newest expert only).

claims.claim: Training is dropout-free in both methods.
claims.detail: ReadoutMoEVQA.train() keeps visual_encoder/text_encoder/text_decoder in eval() unconditionally; LoRA experts contain no dropout; the frozen zero-output vision adapters are not grown by add_expert (only text query/value projections). So phase training consumes torch RNG only through the expert A-init draws.

claims.claim: Fresh-expert training is independent-equivalent in the sense used for the transfer endpoint.
claims.verdict: protocol_equivalent_not_bitwise; two seeded differences remain possible

differences.independent: torch.manual_seed(args.seed) before add_expert at every phase
differences.consequence: different kaiming draws (bitwise) for stream index > 0; same distribution

differences.expansion: epoch_batches rng seed = args.seed + index*1000 + epoch
differences.consequence: different shuffle of the same 2048-image corpus for index > 0
none: per-image reference selection identical per epoch

differences.expansion: frozen siblings numerically inert and no router in phase training (observe happens at phase END, features from LoRA-disabled frozen backbone)
differences.consequence: no numerical effect on the phase's own gradients

claims.claim: The router is the only cross-task knowledge path; it never influences phase training.
claims.detail: Experts occupy disjoint ModuleList slots and only the active expert enters the forward; the gradient guard allows updates only for the current expert. The FeatureRouter refits its ridge boundary at the END of each phase from per-task frozen-feature samples (128 per task, generator-seeded randperm; equal per-task weighting) and at inference only selects an expert per row from image/question features; routing_features disables LoRA and reads no answer/task/family metadata. Hence the new task's expert is trained without router or prior expert influence: cross-task influence is limited to the shared frozen backbone (pretrained) and to eval-time routing of previously-learned and current tasks.
